title: Simulate layout, constraints and user flows
summary: Add deterministic Board scenarios that evaluate component constraints, responsive layouts, navigation flows, source revisions and proposal alternatives before a design change is handed to implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned domain ScenarioPack defines qualified identity, purpose, producer revision, schema version, sensitivity, owner, creation time and expiry.
The initial state is immutable and references exact domain data, configuration, algorithm, capability and artifact revisions with provenance and freshness.
Clock, locale, time zone, random seed, stable IDs, ordering and asynchronous completion controls are explicit where they affect results.
Stimuli and fault injections are ordered, replayable and distinguish user action, system event, external response, delay, failure, cancellation, retry and source change.
Expected invariants, forbidden side effects, observations, decision points, acceptable nondeterminism and completion conditions are represented separately.
Synthetic, recorded, simulator, device, hardware and production-observed evidence classes are labeled and never presented as equivalent proof.
Default replay is isolated, read-only and credential-free; real network, filesystem mutation, hardware control or external action requires a separate approved Work Package.
Baseline and alternatives can be compared from the same scenario inputs through stable observation IDs and explainable differences.
Offline, stale, partial, corrupt, duplicate, reordered, unsupported, cancelled and unavailable states have explicit expected behavior.
Unknown future fields, scenario migration, supersession, corrupted hashes and unsupported schema versions have conservative recovery or refusal behavior.
Scenario output can be exported as a Humble Artifact with content hash, Quality Evidence, source revision and no unrelated sensitive payload.
A deterministic fixture suite and replay tests cover success, failure, interruption, retry, duplicate action, stale input and unsupported version.
Performance and resource budgets are measured against a realistic worst-case fixture without blocking the main UI actor or equivalent runtime.
Scenario execution and results remain repository-owned; HumbleControl receives only normalized references, summaries and explicit handoff artifacts.
The strongest repository-native tests, builds, scenario conformance checks and diff hygiene pass with zero app-owned warnings.
Scenarios cover device-size changes, missing assets, stale source components, variant conflict, broken edge, overflow and unsupported constraint.
Layout observations include frames, constraint violations, overlap, clipping, text expansion, accessibility sizing and unresolved source differences.
Flow scenarios traverse typed navigation edges and record unreachable, cyclic, permission-gated and missing-state paths.
Simulation changes remain Board proposals and cannot mutate repository source or design.json.

agent_notes: Portfolio Intelligence & Simulation Wave 6; evidence-backed scenario and explainable-decision planning ticket.
Estimated effort: L to XL after all prerequisites; split implementation into bounded Work Packages.
Implementation risk: medium-high because deterministic replay, privacy, uncertainty and product decisions must remain honest.
Non-scope: Do not use live production data, real external mutation or model output as ground truth; scenario replay remains isolated and repository-owned.

Alternative considered and rejected: Add a few ad-hoc fixtures to existing tests — rejected because Wave 6 requires versioned state, deterministic stimuli, evidence classes, fault injection and reusable replay artifacts.
Run a fresh delta review against the current default branch before publication or implementation.
Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain-conditional; priority band later. Replay and scenario evidence can reduce risk, but it must follow deterministic core behavior and real evidence.
Wave 10 final rationalization: retain-research-with-cap; portfolio band later. Keep a bounded scenario and decision-support runway where it reduces material risk.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `optional-reference-or-research`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-research`, relevance `later`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `real baseline, deterministic scenario, and no displacement of active delivery`. Replay and simulation can reduce material risk after deterministic behavior and current evidence exist.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-risk-research` / `later` / priority `medium`. Simulation and recommendations follow real product evidence, not precede it.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-research-or-reference`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `later`. Simulation and recommendations follow real product evidence, not precede it.
